title: Updating Single Values and Adding Columns in SQL
summary: Covers the U of CRUD: UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE to change existing records, and ALTER TABLE ... ADD to add a column. Ends with a small challenge that fills a new stock column for two products.

concepts.heading: UPDATE
points: Syntax: UPDATE table SET column = value WHERE condition. UPDATE names the table, SET lists the new values, and WHERE restricts which rows are touched.
Use case: the pencil row was inserted with a NULL price; UPDATE products SET price = 0.8 WHERE id = 2 gives it one.
Danger: without WHERE the statement applies to every row, so UPDATE products SET price = 0.8 would overwrite all prices. Always include WHERE, ideally on the primary key, and check it before running.
(Extra) Several columns can be set in one statement by separating assignments with commas.

concepts.heading: ALTER TABLE ... ADD
points: ALTER TABLE changes the table's structure (add, delete or modify columns) rather than a record.
To add a column give the table name, the ADD keyword, the new column name and its data type: ALTER TABLE products ADD stock INTEGER.
Every existing row receives NULL in the new column, so existing records need a follow-up UPDATE.
The lecture's takeaway: patching in missing columns and back-filling values is tedious, so plan the schema carefully at creation time.

code_examples.caption: Update one row, add a column, back-fill it

task.name: Fill the stock column
task.starting_point: products table with Pen (id 1) and Pencil (id 2). After ALTER TABLE, a stock column exists with NULL in both rows.
task.goal: Give each product its stock count: 32 pens and 12 pencils.
steps: Write UPDATE products SET stock = 32 WHERE id = 1 and run it.
Clear the editor, write UPDATE products SET stock = 12 WHERE id = 2 and run it.
Run SELECT * FROM products to confirm no NULLs remain.
task.expected_result: Pen has stock 32 and Pencil stock 12; pencil price 0.8; no NULL values anywhere.

solution_code.code:
UPDATE products SET stock = 32 WHERE id = 1;
UPDATE products SET stock = 12 WHERE id = 2;

task.reference_repo_path: Section 32 - SQL/32.03 Updating Single Values and Adding Columns in SQL/README.md (text only)

pitfalls: Running UPDATE without WHERE changes every row.
Forgetting that a new column is NULL for existing rows until updated.

gaps_and_ideas: Add to a combined SQL lesson: tasks to fix the NULL price with UPDATE, add stock with ALTER TABLE, back-fill it, then predict what an UPDATE with no WHERE would do before running it.
Demo idea: a 'safety check' toggle that highlights which rows a WHERE will affect before executing an UPDATE.
